mission-board.lede: Daily motion is concentrated in the launch thread. Everything else is either a finished system waiting to be used, or research that outran the decision it was built to inform.
mission-board.next_move: Pick the single thread that can produce a response from outside this system this week, and let the rest sit.
mission-board.caveats: This board counts production, not outcomes — every thread can look busy while nothing reaches a buyer. Stage is inferred from records, so work that happened offline, in conversation, or in another harness reads as idle here.
mission-board.operator_read: Plenty built, little sent — the bottleneck has moved from making to shipping.

linkedin.lede: This is the only thread with live daily motion: campaign support documents, a content cadence, a follow-up plan and a delivery protocol, all written and committed. The offer and the machinery around it exist; nothing recorded here shows a send landing or money changing hands.
linkedin.next_move: Send the next batch of outreach and log what comes back before writing another support document.
linkedin.caveats: Everything captured is production, not response — no reply, call, or payment appears anywhere in this thread's records. The market briefs feeding it run on a schedule and their contribution is unmeasured.
linkedin.operator_read: Fully documented, not yet proven — it's all loading and no firing.

health-performance-ip-library.lede: The daily listening brief is running on schedule and writing into the library, with the exec cut kept current. A gate failure report and an automation-status note also landed, so the loop has been failing visibly rather than silently.
health-performance-ip-library.next_move: Read the gate failure and fix its cause before another day's brief inherits it.
health-performance-ip-library.caveats: The automation runs unattended, so a completed run means it executed — not that the brief was any good. The failure is on record, but nothing shows it was answered.
health-performance-ip-library.operator_read: The listening loop is alive and honest about breaking; someone still has to respond to it.

angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.lede: The listening engine runs end to end — briefs land with vaulted posts and finished carousels attached, living docs get fed, the mirror verifies. Every run scored under the keep line, so the output is usable but not good.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.next_move: Repair the weakest recurring section of the brief format instead of running another cycle on top of it.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.caveats: Scores cluster just below the bar across every run, which usually means a structural flaw in the format rather than a bad day. No downstream result from any vaulted post is recorded.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.operator_read: The engine is dependable; what it produces is consistently mediocre.

01-listing-content.lede: The client listing package reached approval only after a rejected hook pass and a rejected warm-hook version — hooks were rebuilt on interrupt mechanics, then the bodies rewritten as lived scenes. The approved pack is ready to hand over.
01-listing-content.next_move: Send the approved package to the client and stop refining it.

why.0: What's left is polish on supporting formats; the approved spine already carries the delivery, so this is optional and shouldn't hold the send.

01-listing-content.caveats: Approval is recorded on the content, not on results — nothing shows whether it was posted or how it performed. The rejection history points at hook register as the fragile part of this workflow.
01-listing-content.operator_read: Approved and sitting; the only remaining failure mode is not sending it.

farrice-brand.lede: This thread has run as an asset factory — an avatar canon, a character dataset with turnarounds and expressions, acceptance tests, and a wardrobe lane. The identity assets exist; how they get used isn't captured here.
farrice-brand.next_move: Put the locked character assets into an actual published piece and see whether the canon survives contact.
farrice-brand.caveats: Nearly all recorded work is generation rather than deployment, and no record links these assets to a published piece. Acceptance testing was self-run, so 'consistent' means consistent to whoever built it.
farrice-brand.operator_read: The character is fully built and has never appeared in public.

video-studio-edit-bay.lede: The studio was built and shaken down — footage moved through render, captioning and platform exports with no paid tooling in the path. None of the intended pilots have run, so the pipeline is proven on a test clip and nothing else.
video-studio-edit-bay.next_move: Run the first pilot end to end and record the voiceover it asks for.

why.0: The pipeline's real failure modes only surface on actual content — a test clip can't tell you whether the vertical reframe or the stock sourcing is good enough to ship.

video-studio-edit-bay.caveats: Vertical reframing is naive, the stock integrations are untested pending keys, and one cloned component is unwired — all known at build time and none of it exercised since. Nothing produced here has been through a taste pass.
video-studio-edit-bay.operator_read: It renders. Whether it makes anything worth watching is still unknown.

extract-forge.lede: The extraction pipeline is functionally finished — a run of forge-grade expert builds landed, some scored well enough to keep, and the handoff carries no build debt. What remains is a taste verdict, not engineering.
extract-forge.next_move: Run the blind recognition pass only if promoting these extractions would change which ones you actually reach for.

why.0: The open line is a promotion decision rather than missing work — it costs nothing to leave open, but it also keeps the thread from closing.

extract-forge.caveats: Most extractions here logged their outcome as usage-tracked rather than revenue-bearing, which means almost nothing in this thread has been tested against real work. Several builds landed under the keep line and were never revisited.
extract-forge.operator_read: The forge works; the backlog isn't build debt, it's unused output.

04-briefs.lede: The research-brief system shipped and was then re-skinned into the brand's report dialect, with the index and board built around it — both passes scored well enough to keep. The handoff line stored against this thread describes older content-team work, not what actually shipped.
04-briefs.next_move: Route the next reusable deliverable through the brief renderer instead of writing another wall of markdown.
04-briefs.caveats: The stale resume line means anyone picking this thread up loads the wrong context first. Adoption is unmeasured — scoring well is not the same as becoming the default.
04-briefs.operator_read: The brief system is real and good; the line pointing at it is wrong.

system-audit.lede: The work here pushed evidence-backed judgment and pushback into the other harness so meaningful asks stop needing a manual preamble, alongside an after-action record and a verifier. Both passes scored under the keep line and the thread has gone quiet since.
system-audit.next_move: Check whether the judgment-floor change actually holds in live use, then close or park the thread.

why.0: It has been idle long enough that the change is either working silently or was never exercised, and nobody has established which.

system-audit.caveats: One recorded outcome states an earlier audit was never read and a control it recommended was never applied anywhere. Audits produced but unabsorbed is the pattern to watch in this thread specifically.
system-audit.operator_read: Audits keep getting written; whether any of them changed behavior is the open question.

go.lede: This thread holds the cash-launch groundwork — fresh deep research, an adversarial wargame that returned a conditional go, a launch plan and an ICP card — plus the root-cause diagnosis of a failed profile-copy round. It has been idle since the listening engine took over.
go.next_move: Fold its outputs into the live campaign thread or park it, so the launch lives in one place.

why.0: Its outputs are being executed under a different thread while this one still reads as open, which makes the board show the same launch twice.

go.caveats: Nearly every outcome attached here is still pending tracking, so none of the strategy has been checked against a result. The wargame verdict was conditional and whether its fixes were applied is unverified.
go.operator_read: The thinking behind the launch lives here; the launch moved on without closing it.

proof-to-market.lede: The offer layer is written and marked ready — messaging-led, with the search-visibility angle demoted to a module inside it. Nothing moved on it in this window and every mission attached to it closed some time ago.
proof-to-market.next_move: Decide whether this is still the offer being sold, and either put it in front of someone or retire it.
proof-to-market.caveats: There is no recorded activity at all in this window, so the ready status reflects a past decision rather than a current one. Whether it matches what's actively being pitched is unverified.
proof-to-market.operator_read: Shelf-ready and untouched — treat its ready flag as history until someone pitches it.
